stem: Meera's grandmother says that the small intestine is only a thin tube that passes food to the large intestine. Meera explains that the small intestine does much more. Which row of the table correctly describes what happens in the small intestine?

options.text: receives digestive secretions ✓; basic pancreatic juice neutralises acidic food ✓; carbohydrates, proteins and fats digested ✓; nutrients absorbed into blood ✓
receives digestive secretions ✓; basic pancreatic juice neutralises acidic food ✗; carbohydrates, proteins and fats digested ✓; nutrients absorbed into blood ✗
receives digestive secretions ✗; basic pancreatic juice neutralises acidic food ✓; carbohydrates, proteins and fats digested ✓; nutrients absorbed into blood ✓

teacher.key_rationale: The small intestine receives secretions from its own lining, the liver and the pancreas; basic pancreatic juice neutralises the acidic food from the stomach; it completes digestion of carbohydrates, proteins and fats; and the digested nutrients pass into blood vessels in its walls. So all four statements are true, matching row A. Rows B, C and D each drop one or more of these functions, consistent with students who treat the small intestine as merely a passage tube.
